To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
paraffin-embedding of tissue sections is a useful way to obtain control DNA for forensic purposes.
paraffin- embedded tissues can be used for DNA isolation and that this method is suitable for solving of crime cases.

1) the method of DNA isolation from paraffin- embedded tissues was elaborated; 2) its usefulness was tested and the yield of the DNA from the histological section of the tissue was sufficient for further analyses; 3) the method was successfully used for the solution of concrete crime cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using paraffin-embedding as a source of DNA for the purposes of forensic genetics.
the development of a new technique for the isolation of DNA from paraffin-embedding tissue.
the elaboration of a simple method for the isolation of DNA from paraffin- embedded histopathological preparations, and with its application in forensic medicine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
paraffin-embeded tissues are an excellent source of the control DNA.
paraffin-embedding of tissues is not a serious barrier in the isolation of DNA from them and, consequently, it is not a barrier in forensic DNA analysis.
the method of isolation of DNA from paraffin- embedded tissue sections is simple and reliable and it may be applied in forensic practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

paraffin- embedded tissues are a good source of DNA, and the isolation procedure elaborated by us allows to obtain DNA in sufficient amount from one section of such a tissue, and the DNA is suitable for further analysis.
paraffin-embeded tissue can be a useful source of control DNA.
it is possible to use paraffin-embedding for DNA extraction, and it is also possible to use DNA extracted from paraffin-embeddings for forensic DNA analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
paraffin-embedding does not affect the quality of DNA, which is suitable for the purposes of forensic DNA analysis.
the paraffin embedded tissues can be a source of control samples of DNA in forensic cases.
paraffin-embedding of tissues can be used as a source of DNA for forensic purposes.
